source.title: John Hancock begins a new legacy with digital experiences

source_facts.fact: Prospective life-insurance customers can obtain a quote, submit an application, and sign through a portal.
Most previously manual application processing steps were automated.
Long-term-care customers can submit service claims online and upload receipt images.
Customer information formerly spread across multiple systems was brought into a unified view.
A legacy data store is connected while minimizing unnecessary data replication.

validation_extensions.scenario: An expired or changed synthetic quote requires explicit application reconfirmation.
Two browser tabs submit the same synthetic application and receive one application number.
Duplicate, late, and out-of-order signature callbacks advance state once and retain raw evidence.
Decline, additional-information, and approval paths enforce state, permission, and notification boundaries.
A repeated synthetic receipt business key cannot create two payable claim items.
Binary and metadata transaction failure is compensated or detected by orphan scanning.
Legacy provider unavailability exposes recovery state without overwriting known customer facts.
Retention expiry, legal hold, and audited export cover synthetic application and claim data.

synthetic_data_policy: Use fictional applicants, claimants, quotes, applications, signatures, policies, receipt metadata, and provider responses; never copy real PII, claims, or receipt images.
